summary: readFileAtRef probes with --literal-pathspecs, so a path git spelled is matched as a path and never parsed as pathspec magic
acceptance: a committed path beginning with ':' reads back its content at the ref, and reaches the revert snapshot
tests: readFileAtRef reads a committed path whose name begins with a colon
snapshotReverted writes a colon-leading path's content into the revert snapshot
notes: Measured git 2.43: the probe parses ':leading.ts' as pathspec magic — empty listing, so readFileAtRef returns null for a path present at the ref and snapshotReverted's null-skip silently drops it; ':(icase)x' exits 128 instead, losing the whole snapshot. The note's glob half ('*', '?', '[') did not reproduce — ls-tree matched no wildcard on 2.43 — so scope is the leading colon.
